title: On a statement of A. N. Shoshitaishvili about weighted homogeneous singularities
description: Let F be a weighted homogeneous polynomial with an isolated critical point at 0, with weights w_1 >= ... >= w_n and degree d. Statement 1 of the author's 1976 paper says that if phi(0)=0 and the Jacobian ideal of phi lies in the Jacobian ideal of F, then phi lies in the Jacobian ideal of F and has weighted degree at least d. The second part is equivalent to the absence of nonzero derivations of negative weight of the Milnor algebra of F; since 1995 Shoshitaishvili's Statement 1 has been studied as a conjecture of S. S.-T. Yau, and as the Milnor-algebra case of Halperin's conjecture. We describe the history of the statement and give a proof of the following: with M = min(w_3 - 2w_n, w_1 - 3w_n), the Milnor algebra has no nonzero derivation of weight -q if q > M, or if q > M - (w_{n-1} - w_n) and w_n does not divide d - q; in particular it has no nonzero derivation of negative weight when w_3 <= 2w_n or w_1 <= 3w_n.
